description: totalReviewScore() calls Array.prototype.reduce with no initial value, which throws a TypeError on an empty array — a real, reachable crash if a pull request can have zero reviews, which the function's own doc comment implies is possible ('every review on a pull request').

required_findings.justification: Array.prototype.reduce, called with only a callback and no initial/seed value, throws 'TypeError: Reduce of empty array with no initial value' when called on an empty array. This function's own contract ('every review on a pull request') implies `scores` can legitimately be empty (a PR with no reviews yet) — a plausible, non-adversarial input this function does not handle, fully verifiable from the reduce() call's arity and JavaScript's own documented behavior for that case, with no external assumption required.

explanation: Deliberately combines two of the benchmark's target categories in one fixture: this is simultaneously an edge-case-handling defect (empty array not handled) and a textbook API-misuse pattern (reduce without an initial value) — both are equally valid, correct framings of the SAME root cause, which is why both categories are allowed rather than picking one as the only correct label. Severity is P1: a live crash on a plausible, easily-reachable input (zero reviews) rather than a merely theoretical one.
